title: Opera Omnia S. Maximus Confessor 1 (Migne P.G. 90)
author: Maximus the Confessor
description: Opera Omnia of St Maximus the Confessor, Volume 1, from Jacques-Paul Migne's Patrologia Graeca, volume 90 (Paris, 1865), the Greek texts with Latin translation. Maximus (c. 580-662), Byzantine monk and theologian, defended the doctrine of Christ's two wills against Monothelitism, suffering mutilation and exile, and is regarded as one of the greatest theologians of the Eastern Church. This volume opens with the ancient lives and acts of Maximus and contains major works including the Questions to Thalassius (Quaestiones ad Thalassium), a deep spiritual exegesis of difficult passages of scripture; the commentary on the Lord's Prayer; and the Chapters on Love and the Chapters on Theology and the Economy of the Incarnation, among other treatises. Maximus's teaching on the logoi of creation, cosmic liturgy and deification shaped Byzantine mystical theology and the Philokalia.
